name: Eva Bhandari
life: “I still remember scrubbing adverts off a wall to make room for a local artist.” Saturday often includes a stop at the approach to Seabright Court, where Eva likes to watch the beach traffic thin enough for workers going the other way.
voice: I own the wall where the advert would hang. I would rather use it for a local exhibition of working hands.
appearance: Eva has soft white hair brushed sideways, a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow, and a favorite piece of clothing, a long navy raincoat. It usually goes with a cloth patch so neatly matched it only shows in strong light. When somebody else has the floor, Eva turns fully toward the person speaking.
personality: Eva talks very little about private fear and recognizes it quickly in strangers. Offering a choice of seats is one of Eva's ways of saying that it is all right to leave.
agenda: To reserve the wall for working hands with permission.
family: Selena Sáenz is Eva’s younger cousin. Eva chooses whether to use it. Selena saves a place. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *Level with the window*, Selena says, “I manage the detour and have never had a route run through somebody's supper before.”
connections: Louise Hooper. The studio assistant and the wall owner discuss giving local workers their own credits.

reactions.situation: The model asks to see the unedited print
reactions.response: Eva gets the model a private look before anybody else comments on the hand.

reactions.situation: An unfamiliar person asks for directions but cannot read the street signs
reactions.response: Eva draws the route by its turns and entrances and has the person show which turn comes first.

reactions.situation: When pressed to explain someone else's silence
reactions.response: Eva says only what happened and lets the absent person keep their reasons.
